TDNN weights (asymptotic, k = 1), distance-based ranking

Source: R/api-weights.R
weights_tdnn_asymp.Rd

Computes Demirkaya two-scale DNN (TDNN) weights using the asymptotic rank-weight table (tdnn_rank_table_asymp()) over all n ranks. Weights may be negative or exactly zero through signed cancellation or underflow.

Usage

weights_tdnn_asymp(
  X,
  X0 = NULL,
  x0 = NULL,
  distance = "l2",
  s1,
  s2,
  dim = NULL,
  normalize = TRUE,
  ctx = NULL,
  return = c("W")
)

Arguments

X

Numeric matrix (n x p).

X0

Numeric matrix (m x p); mutually exclusive with x0.

x0

Numeric length-p single target (convenience for m = 1).

distance

Distance spec or registered name (e.g., "l2").

s1

Positive integer; smaller U-statistic order (s1 < s2 <= n).

s2

Positive integer; larger U-statistic order.

dim

Positive integer; localization dimension. Defaults to ncol(X) when NULL.

normalize

Logical; renormalize rank table columns to sum 1 (default TRUE).

ctx

Optional context passed through to distance and rank-weight evaluators.

return

Character vector of extras to include; any of c("W", "ord", "ranks", "dx").

Value

A rdistnn_weights_result object (same structure as weights_dnn_asymp()).

Numerical limits

Asymptotic intervals use host Beta probabilities. At subnormal scales, endpoint rounding can erase an interval or change its zero/nonzero support; R and the Stata companion can disagree. Signed TDNN combinations can amplify component rounding. These extreme-tail limitations remain unresolved. Normalization or switching the R/compiled deletion engine does not recover probability mass already lost during table construction. Exact and asymptotic weights are different constructions; changing the method changes the localization rule.

Exact distance ties

For each target, observations with exactly equal computed distance share the average of their assigned rank weights, including distinct covariate vectors. Equality is exact represented equality, without an epsilon or rounding. Groups may differ by target. Block mass is preserved for signed and unnormalized rules. Equal distances are ordered by original row index. A bare supplied rank or order matrix defines a strict order and is not averaged. A list containing ranks or orders together with dx preserves that authoritative permutation and averages by the supplied distances. No outcomes, treatments or nuisance values define membership.

For a block at ranks a:b, each member receives sum(w_n[a:b]) / (b-a+1). Estimator jackknife deletions remove the actual observation, update ranks, and average remaining blocks with w_(n-1). If a member is deleted, each survivor receives sum(w_(n-1)[a:(b-1)]) / (b-a); a deleted singleton contributes zero. Exact support edges describe the unaveraged rank table; averaging can extend nonzero observation weights through a block crossing that edge. Lower-level rank-only APIs retain their rank-primitive semantics.

A warning is emitted once per public call with distance ties. The accompanying theory assumes a continuous distance distribution and does not establish inference under persistent ties, including for k = 1.

See also

weights_tdnn_exact(), weights_tdnn(), rank_weight_tdnn_asymp()

Examples

set.seed(1)
X  <- matrix(rnorm(30), 15, 2)
x0 <- c(0, 0)
out <- weights_tdnn_asymp(X, x0 = x0, s1 = 3L, s2 = 6L)
colSums(out$W)  # 1
#> [1] 1
